statements.statement: P-ceil (ceiling of information floors; under: none). Premises: any positive table on C classes, any weights, any k. Let s_x >= e sbar with e in (0,1], and let g be any per-unit charge with g(e) >= 1 - e. Then I(s) - k g(e) <= (1 - e)(H(sbar) - k) <= (1 - e)(log C - k). So a floor of the form I(s') - k g(e'), on the table itself or on any table s' derived from it on at most C classes, is <= 0 once k >= log C, for every admissible e'. This covers: K2 (g = log(1/e)); K2b(a), which gives <= alpha (1 - u)(H(sbar) - k) with u = e/alpha; K2b(d) minors, each term <= w_b (1 - e_b)(log|H_b| - k); TQ19 lumps (C' <= C); and every soft-e or truncated table, since any charge for the moved mass only subtracts more. At C = 1000 such a floor is empty at every k >= 7. Positive needs C > e^k, which is 1.2 million classes at k = 14. It does NOT cover a charge below 1 - e: K4's charge (1/2) log(1/(e(2 - e))) is below 1 - e for e above about .07, so K4 in general stays open. At the real e = 2.9e-9, K4's charge is 9.47 nats per unit, above 1 - e, so the conclusion holds on this table.
statements.proof: Write s_x = e sbar + (1 - e) r_x. r_x >= 0 by the definition of e, it sums to 1, and sum p_x r_x = sbar. Joint convexity of KL gives KL(s_x || sbar) <= (1 - e) KL(r_x || sbar). Average over x: I(s) <= (1 - e) I(r). I(r) = H(sbar) - H(r | x) <= H(sbar) <= log C. So I(s) - k g(e) <= (1 - e) H(sbar) - k (1 - e). For K2 use log(1/e) >= 1 - e. K2b(a): I(s) - (1 - alpha) I(r) - alpha k log(alpha/e) <= (alpha - e) I(r) - alpha k log(1/u) = alpha [(1 - u) I(r) - k log(1/u)] <= alpha (1 - u)(H(sbar) - k). QED. Read as a network: a unit can lose at most about 1 - e of a nat of what it keeps, and N has at most log C nats to lose.

statements.statement: Soft e cannot be repaired by a charge on the moved mass (method statement, not a result about networks). No bound of the form L_free(k) >= I(s) - k log(1/u) - Ch(u, mu(u)) holds for k >= 2 with Ch finite and independent of C, where mu(u) = sum p_x sum_i (u sbar[i] - s_x[i])_+. A charge must grow like (1 - u) log C. The cause: a class a row finds unlikely can be pushed down at almost no cost, so the mass below a level gives no constraint on the codes.
statements.proof: Rows x = 1..C, p = 1/C, s_x = (1 - eps) delta_x + eps/C on every class. sbar is uniform and mu(u) <= u. Take class points b_i on a circle, t = 0, c_x = M b_x, g = 1 - cos(2 pi / C), M = log(C / sqrt(eps)) / g. Then the mass of q_x off class x is at most about sqrt(eps), and the tail term of KL is at most eps * 2M. So L_free(2) tends to 0 as eps tends to 0 at fixed C, while I(s) tends to log C. At fixed u the right side is then about log C - k log(1/u) - Ch, which exceeds 0 for large C if Ch is bounded. QED.

statements.statement: P-coup (a certified coupling for every head; B3 of round 1, re-proved in K1's frame; under: none; NOT refereed). Rows x, weights p_x, s_x > 0, n_xi = p_x s_x[i], T = log s. Let R, H be rows and classes with |H| >= k + 2, a > 0 on R, b > 0 on H with sum b = 1, and a_x b_i <= n_xi on R x H. Let That be T on R x H with the b-mean of each row subtracted, then the a-weighted mean of each column. r_x^2 = sum_i b_i That_xi^2, beta = max a_x sqrt(b_i) r_x / n_xi, M = D_a^(1/2) That D_b^(1/2), E = sum over j > k of sigma_j^2(M). R(beta) = max over 0 < tau <= 1/beta of tau - (tau^2 / 2)(1 + tau beta). Then the least of the minor R x H at k units is >= R(beta) E. For a list of blocks with disjoint class sets on each row, TQ22 adds these, each with its own beta. Overlapping layers with sum of a b <= n, one common beta and the sum of E also hold, and the same proof works. For any head V this builds a coupling of K1 with higher entropy than s, so it is a floor of the form I(s) - I(pi) with pi depending on V.
statements.proof: Fix a competitor (t, V, c). Pi is the L2(b)-orthogonal projector on R^H onto the complement of 1 and V restricted to H. g_x = Pi That_x. For tau <= 1/beta let delta_xi = -(tau / p_x) a_x b_i g_xi, zero off the block, and pi_x = s_x + delta_x. (1) Pi_x is a distribution: <g, 1>_b = 0, and |g_xi| <= r_x / sqrt(b_i), so |delta_xi| / s_xi <= tau beta <= 1. (2) Moments: V^T delta_x = 0, because g is b-orthogonal to V on H. (3) Marginal: sum p_x delta_x = -tau b Pi (sum a_x That_x) = 0, by the a-weighted column centring. So pi is a coupling of K1. (4) K1 gives D >= sum p_x [H(pi_x) - H(s_x)] = sum p_x [-<delta_x, T_x> - KL(pi_x || s_x)]. On H, T_x is That_x plus a row constant plus a vector free of x, and both integrate out. So the first term is tau sum a_x |g_x|_b^2 =: tau E'. (5) Cost: with v = delta / s, phi(v) = (1 + v) log(1 + v) - v <= v^2 / 2 for v >= 0, and <= (r^2 + r^3) / 2 for v = -r. So KL cost <= ((1 + tau beta) / 2) sum (p_x delta_xi)^2 / n_xi, and (a b g)^2 <= n_xi a b g^2 by a b <= n. So cost <= (tau^2 / 2)(1 + tau beta) E'. Thus D >= E' R(beta). (6) E' = |M Pi~|_F^2 with Pi~ removing sqrt(b) and at most k more directions, and M sqrt(b) = 0, so E' >= E by Eckart-Young. Per-minor beta: the minor has n'_xi = p_x s_x[i] = n_xi, and its T differs by a row constant, so the block value on the raw table equals the value on the minor. QED.

statements.statement: P3 (the rate identity: why product couplings stay small; under: none). For a layer with a_x b_i <= n_xi let c_xi = n_xi / (a_x b_i) >= 1, y = log c, m_x = sum_i n_xi. Then (a) the double-centred T equals the double-centred y; (b) a_x = m_x / E_b[c_x]; (c) |M|_F^2 <= sum_x a_x Var_b(y_x) = sum_x m_x Var_b(y_x) / E_b[e^(y_x)]; (d) Var(y) / E[e^y] <= 4 / e^2 for y >= 0. So the method has no universal barrier in (d), and everything depends on the real shape of y. REAL VALUES, ResNet-18, 125 blocks of 200 class rows by 40 classes, tight a: block mass 1.000; minorant mass sum a_x = .0036; mass-weighted Var_b(y) = 5.7; mass-weighted log E_b[c] = 8.2; identity value .00848; |M|_F^2 = .00825; f = E / |M|_F^2 = .184; E = .00152; mass-weighted beta 21.6, R about .044; floor at tight a 7.4e-5, 1.33e-4 after row scales. ResNet-50: .0021, 6.3, 9.0, .0053, .0052, .174, 8.99e-4, 22.4, 4.3e-5. THE REASON THE VALUE STAYS NEAR 0: the loss is in the step E_b[c], a factor of about 280 on mass. Even at R = 1 the E available is 16 times short of the target. Network reading: in a block of 200 class rows by 40 classes, each row's own class and relatives sit about e^8 above the product shape, and the coupling must stay under every entry, so it moves about 1/280 of the mass.
statements.proof: (a) T_xi = log a_x + log b_i + y_xi - log p_x, and double centring kills row and column constants. (b) m_x = sum a_x b_i c_xi. (c) Double centring is an orthogonal projection in the a-tensor-b metric, so the norm falls, and the first centring gives Var_b. (d) y^2 <= (4 / e^2) e^y for y >= 0, since y^2 e^(-y) is largest at y = 2. QED.

statements.statement: P1 (a second block floor; under: none). On R x H with a_x b_i <= n_xi and M as in P-coup, for every tau > 0, with kappa = 2 psi(-tau) / tau^2 and psi(e) = e^e - 1 - e: the minor's least at k is >= min over r >= 0 of [ psi(-tau) * (sum of the r smallest n_xi) + (kappa / 2) sum over j > k + r of sigma_j^2(M) ]. Measured: dominated. It beat P-coup on 43 of 280 configurations, by at most 2.8 times, and never at the best one. Its best is 1.64e-5 on R18 at k = 14.
statements.proof: Let e_xi = log(q_xi / s_xi) on the minor; the loss is sum n psi(e) (B1). L = T' + e is t + V c plus row offsets. Let C be the double centring by sqrt(a), sqrt(b); it is an orthogonal projection on matrices. Then C(D_a^.5 L D_b^.5) has rank <= k, since the offsets and t die. Let S = {e < -tau}, r = |S|, and split G = D_a^.5 e D_b^.5 = G1 + G2 with G2 on S, so rank C(G2) <= r. M - C(G1) = C(D_a^.5 L D_b^.5) - C(G2) has rank <= k + r. So the tail of M past k + r is at most |G1|_F^2. psi(e)/e^2 increases in e, so off S, n psi(e) >= a b kappa e^2 / 2. On S, psi falls on negatives, so n psi(e) >= n psi(-tau). Sum, then minimise over r. QED.

statements.statement: Q-A (the fixed-V dual, and H1's row cap is the same set). Fix V of rank <= k. For free codes, the least over (t, c) of D equals the max of sum p_x [H(q°_x) - H(s_x)] over rows q°_x in the simplex with V^T (q°_x - s_x) = 0 for each x and sum p_x (q°_x - s_x) = 0. Now take H1's row form with a tail number e and top class tau(x): q°_xi = e y_xi / p_x on the tail, q°_x,tau = 1 - e y_x / p_x. The conditions y >= 0 and the row cap e y_x <= p_x say exactly that q°_x >= 0. So the row-weighted form of H1 removes no dual point and adds no dual point. At fixed V it gives the exact value. Its only open step is the inf over V. A per-row e_x changes the parametrisation only.
statements.proof: The problem in (t, c) is convex and q° = s is a strictly positive feasible point of the dual, so Fenchel duality holds with no gap. Gibbs gives log sum exp(l) >= <q°, l> + H(q°). So KL(s || softmax l) >= H(q°) - H(s) + <q° - s, l>. The constraints make the sum of the last term over rows 0 for every l = t + V c. At a minimiser, q° = softmax(l) gives equality. The H1 identity is a change of variables. The envelope of H1 (m + 1) v0 - hbar drops the entropy of q°. At mean tail .31 that dropped term makes the value negative, as the referee found.

statements.statement: Q-B (the sharp worst entry of a projected vector). Let u be a unit vector in R^K, g perp u, and e' = e_i - u_i u, so |e'|^2 = 1 - u_i^2. Over all orthogonal projectors Pi on u-perp, the range of (Pi g)_i is exactly [(g_i - |e'||g|)/2, (g_i + |e'||g|)/2]. Both ends are attained with P of rank 1 inside u-perp.
statements.proof: Put v = Pi e'. Then <v, e'> = |v|^2, so v lies on the sphere with centre e'/2 and radius |e'|/2. Also (Pi g)_i = <v, g>, since g perp u gives <e', g> = g_i. Cauchy on the sphere gives both bounds. To attain: let v = e'/2 -+ |e'| g / (2 |g|) and w = e' - v. Then v perp w, so the projector off w maps e' to v. With scale gamma and V column w / gamma, a real competitor with k >= 1 realises it.

statements.statement: Q-C (the weighted rectangle dual, computable at any k). Rows x, weights p_x, table s > 0, n = p s, A = log s. A system is a family b of rectangles R x S, |S| = K, with weights W^b_xi > 0 on R x S and sum over b of W^b_xi <= n_xi at every entry. Each b also has a scale gamma > 0 on S, u = gamma / |gamma|, fixed vectors g_x perp gamma, and numbers rho_x in (0, 1]. Cap: gamma_i (sqrt(1 - u_i^2) |g_x| - g_xi) / 2 <= rho_x W_xi for all x, i. Let kap(rho) = ((1 - rho) log(1 - rho) + rho) / rho^2, kap(1) = 1, m_x = max_i gamma_i^2 / W_xi, f_x = gamma * A_x with its gamma part removed, B_b = -sym(sum g_x f_x^T) - sum kap(rho_x) m_x g_x g_x^T. Then L_free(k) >= sum_b [tr B_b - the sum of the k + 1 largest positive eigenvalues of B_b]. With kept units T, replace k + 1 by k + 1 + |T|. Three uses are computed. Q1: entry-disjoint rectangles with W = n. Q5: flat slices, W = p (t_l - t_(l+1)) on entries with s >= t_l. Then the cap holds with no entry of s in it, and the sum over slices is at most s. Q7: all rows on one class-tree node, W^N_xi = alpha_x(N), the row's least leftover on the node.
statements.proof: psi(e) = exp(e) - 1 - e >= 0, so D = sum n psi(e) >= sum_b sum W^b psi(e), with e = log q - A = L - A and L_x = t + V c_x - log Z_x. On S, L_x lies in span(t_S, V_S, 1_S). Let Pi be the orthogonal projector off gamma times this span. Its P part in gamma-perp has rank <= k + 1. Put Y_xi = gamma_i (Pi g_x)_i, h = Y / W. Q-B and the cap give h >= -rho_x for every competitor. Fenchel: W psi(e) >= Y e - W psi*(h), psi*(h) = (1 + h) log(1 + h) - h. psi*(h) / h^2 is decreasing in h (Bennett's function), so psi*(h) <= kap(rho) h^2 for h >= -rho. <Y_x, L_x> = <Pi g_x, gamma * L_x> = 0. So the block's sum is at least sum_x [-<Pi g_x, f_x> - kap m_x |Pi g_x|^2] = tr(Pi B). B vanishes on gamma. The inf over projectors of tr(Pi B) with rank P <= k + 1 on gamma-perp is tr B minus the k + 1 largest positive eigenvalues. Sum over b. QED.

statements.statement: Q-D (the entropy form). In Q1 with W = n and p_x, set r_x = s_x + gamma * g_x on S and q° = s + gamma * Pi g = r - gamma * P g. The row's term is exactly p [H_S(q°) - H_S(s)], and it is at least p [H_S(r) - H_S(s) + <gamma * log r, P g> - kap m |P g|^2], m = max_i gamma_i^2 / r_xi, kap = kap(rho), rho = max_i gamma_i (g_i + sqrt(1 - u_i^2) |g|) / (2 r_xi) <= 1. So the rectangle gives sum p [H_S(r) - H_S(s)] minus the sum of the k + 1 largest positive eigenvalues of sum p [-sym(g (gamma * log r)^T) + kap m g g^T].
statements.proof: The Fenchel term with y = q° - s, sum y = 0, <y, L> = 0 equals H_S(q°) - H_S(s), and log s cancels: this is A's cancellation in general form. Then H_S(q°) = H_S(r) - <log r, q° - r> - d(q° || r). And d(a || b) = b psi*((a - b) / b) <= kap (a - b)^2 / b for a >= (1 - rho) b. QED.

statements.statement: Q-E (the ceiling on one rectangle, W = n, fixed gamma). Let a dual Y_x(V) = gamma * Pi_V g_x with fixed g_x stay >= -s_x at every competitor. Let a_i = 2 s_xi / gamma_i sorted, e* = sqrt(1 - max u_i^2). Then |g_x| <= Gamma_x = the least over j >= 2 with e* > 1 / sqrt j of a_(j) / (e* - 1 / sqrt j). The moved mass is mu_x <= |gamma| Gamma_x / 2. For any choice of g, the rectangle's inf over V is at most sum p [mu log(K - 1) + M h(mu / M)], M = the row's mass on S, h = binary entropy. So all duals linear in the projector are capped by the rows' j-th least ratio s_xi / gamma_i, for the gamma in use.
statements.proof: Q-B gives g_i >= sqrt(1 - u_i^2) |g| - a_i for each i. If |g| > a_(j) / (e* - 1 / sqrt j), the j smallest a_i each give g_i > |g| / sqrt j, so the sum of g_i^2 exceeds |g|^2, a contradiction. Cauchy: |y|_1 <= |gamma| |g|. At V = 0, t = 0, Pi is the identity on gamma-perp, so the value there is p [H_S(s + y) - H_S(s)]. Audenaert's bound on entropy against total variation (2007), applied on S with mass M, gives the rest. The inf over V is at most this value. QED.

statements.statement: Q-F (the block ceiling). Consider any certificate of the form D >= sum_b D_b with weights sum W^b <= n, where D_b reads only rectangle b and is valid for every L of rank at most k + 2 on b with 1 in its row space. Then sum_b D_b <= sum_b inf over such L of sum W^b psi(L - A). If the rectangles lie inside row groups R_g, then sum_b D_b <= the sum over g of the least of the problem on the rows of R_g with its own k units. This is TQ22's sentence 'each minor gets all k units', and the mechanism of I8-F, stated for every dual of this form.
statements.proof: For each b, D_b <= its value at any allowed L, and Fenchel gives value <= sum W^b psi(L - A). Each L may differ per b, because D_b reads only b. For row groups, sum over b inside g of W^b psi(e) <= D on the rows of g at that group's competitor. QED.

statements.statement: Q-G (coverage of slice systems). In a slice t, a flat rectangle of useful size lies inside the (k + 2, k + 3)-core of the graph {s_xi >= t}: remove rows with fewer than k + 3 entries and classes with fewer than k + 2 entries until stable. So in a slice system, with rectangles entry-disjoint inside each slice, the covered mass is at most C = the sum over slices of p d_l |core_l|.
statements.proof: Q-C.1 gives the size floor. A rectangle with all entries in the graph survives the pruning, since each of its rows has at least |S| entries and each of its classes has at least |R| entries. Entry-disjoint rectangles in a slice cover at most |core_l| entries. QED.

statements.statement: Row drop does not rescue the cap (Theorem Q4). Let a row be active at a competitor iff |P g_x| <= tau_x, tau_x = the least r_xi / gamma_i, r = s + gamma * g, and give an inactive row dual 0. Then D >= tr B - the sum of the k + 1 largest positive eigenvalues of B + E, E = sum over rows that are not always active of (w_x / tau_x^2) g_x g_x^T, with w_x any upper bound of the row's term over all P. The inequality is proved. It charges a competitor-dependent row selection through a linear term in P. On real tables it gives no measured gain. The reason: on a row with tiny entries, lifting them to a floor moves about as much mass as the floor holds, so tau / |g| is about 1 / (2 sqrt K), while one projector of rank k + 1 captures at least (k + 1) / K of the rows' energy on average when the rows span K dimensions. That average is about 4 (k + 1) times too large. This reason is an estimate, not a theorem.
statements.proof: Inequality: for an inactive row, 1 <= |P g_x|^2 / tau_x^2, so the dropped term is at most w_x |P g_x|^2 / tau_x^2 = tr(P (w_x / tau_x^2) g g^T). The active terms use Q-B's bound G_i + tau in place of the sphere. Add over rows. QED. No-gain: measured only.

statements.statement: The reason the bound is small, as a statement about the table. On the class-row table at k = 14, a dual linear in the projector has three losses, in this order on R18: coverage 17.5 times, fresh rank per block 14.5 times, cap 3.4 times. (a) Rows disagree. There is no 16 by 17 flat rectangle above t = 1.8e-3 (Q-G), and greedy finds no 24 by 17 rectangle above t about 3e-4. The mass in useful rectangles is under .01 by greedy and at most .10 in slice systems. The table's top class holds .58, and the entries the fit gets wrong are in the row-specific part. (b) Each rectangle has its own k + 2 ranks, which leave RMS .58 of log s on the covered entries, while the shared 14 units leave a loss of 2.6 per unit of covered mass. (c) One projector can aim a row's whole move at one class (Q-B), so relative moves have RMS about 2 / sqrt K. Bigger rectangles would charge sharing, but they exist only at low t, where their weight is small. Sweeping rectangle size, row groups and tree nodes moved the bound only between 7e-4 and 1.2e-3 of the fit.

The three factors multiply along the measured chain .2452, .01403, .00097, 2.885e-4. The chain's second number is the fit's loss, and the fit is an upper value of L_table, so 'one set of units serving all blocks' describes this fit and is not proved for the true least.

result.blocked_by: Ky Fan needs tr(Pi B), linear in one projector, and one projector needs one class scale gamma shared by all rows of the block. Rows differ by a largest log-ratio of 39, so the shared scale forces one of two losses: a tiny common weight on a big block (Q1, Q-E), or small flat blocks with fresh rank on each (Q5, Q7, Q-F). A row's own metric would avoid both, but then the inf over V is weighted low-rank approximation, with no computable value. Likewise the walled form of H1 is exact at each V (Q-A) and its inf over V is the walled program, with no bound at k = 14. The step that stops me: I have no dual nonlinear in the projector whose inf over V has a computable lower bound.

verdicts.statement: P-ceil: a floor I(s') - k g(e') with g(e') >= 1 - e' is at most (1 - e')(H(sbar') - k), so it is empty once k >= log C. At C = 1000 this means every k >= 7.
verdicts.false_step: None in the proof. I checked the mixture split, joint convexity, I(r) <= H(sbar), log(1/e) >= 1 - e, and the K2b(a) algebra. One side number is wrong: K4's charge falls below 1 - e at e = .0834, not at about .07.
verdicts.counterexample: None to the theorem. Side numbers: at e = .07 the charge is 1.0009 and 1 - e is .93, so the charge is still above 1 - e. Summary wording: the ceiling is -7.12 (1 - e), so it is -6.40 at e = .1, and it is not -7.12 at every e.
verdicts.gaps: 1. The clause on soft or truncated tables covers only floors that pass through a table s' with its own I(s'). A direct form I(s) - k log(1/u) - Ch is not covered by this proof. The corrected soft-e verdict below closes that form on the real tables. 2. The item in 'next' that says K4 needs e above about .017 is false. See the corrected statement. 3. 'Nearly all of a marginal' overstates mu(u)/u, which is .69 to .88 at u = .1 to .7 on ResNet-18.
verdicts.corrected_statement: Keep P-ceil and add this. Any K4-form term obeys I(s') - (k/2) log(1/(e(2 - e))) <= (1 - e) log C' - (k/2) log(1/(e(2 - e))). At k = 14 this is positive only for e > .290 at C' = 1000, e > .448 at C' = 100, e > .533 at C' = 40. At k = 38, C' = 1000 it needs e > .658. At k = 7, C' = 1000 it needs e > .086. The author's best screened e is .069. So at k = 14 even the conjectured K4 is empty on these minors. The same inequality with a weight w_b applies to each minor.

verdicts.statement: Soft e cannot be repaired by a charge: no bound L_free(k) >= I(s) - k log(1/u) - Ch(u, mu(u)) holds for k >= 2 with Ch finite and independent of C. A charge must grow like (1 - u) log C.
verdicts.false_step: The first sentence is true, but the author's proof excludes only a bounded Ch. On the family, mu changes with C, because u - mu is about u/C. So a finite Ch that is unbounded as mu tends to u passes the proof. The rate '(1 - u) log C' is also wrong.
verdicts.counterexample: Proof gap: Ch = 1/(u - mu) is finite and free of C, and the author's family does not contradict it, because on that family Ch is about C/u. Rate: at C = 1000, u = .5, k = 2, the family needs Ch >= log C - k log(1/u) = 5.52 in the limit eps -> 0, while (1 - u) log C = 3.45.
verdicts.gaps: This is a method statement on a toy family. It is not a round result and it fills nothing. I checked the competitor by hand and by code: at C = 64, eps = 1e-9, KL = 4.0e-6 and I = 4.1589.
verdicts.corrected_statement: Repair. Add flat rows of total weight lam with s = uniform and c = 0. The other rows are the author's rows. Then L_free(2) -> 0 as eps -> 0, I -> (1 - lam) log C, and mu -> (1 - lam) u (1 - 1/C). Checked at C = 1000, lam = .5: KL 5.3e-7, I 3.4539. So at each fixed u and 0 < mu < u, a valid Ch(u, mu, C) must be at least (mu/u) log C - k log(1/u). No finite C-free Ch exists at any such point. Real-table evaluation: with Ch >= 0, the floor is at most min(I - k log(1/u), I - (mu/u) log C). Largest value over a 400-point u grid: k = 14: -1.27 on ResNet-18, -1.03 on ResNet-50. k = 3: -.50, -.34. k = 2: -.0068, +.14. So the charged soft-e form is empty at k >= 3 on both nets.

verdicts.statement: P-coup: for a block with a_x b_i <= n_xi, the least of the minor at k units is at least R(beta) E. TQ22 adds blocks with disjoint class sets on each row. Overlapping layers hold with one common beta and the sum of E.
verdicts.false_step: None in the single-layer proof. I checked each step by hand: row sums, positivity from |g_xi| <= r_x / sqrt(b_i), moments, marginal from a-weighted column centring, the entropy identity, cost, and Eckart-Young with M sqrt(b) = 0. phi(-r) <= (r^2 + r^3)/2 follows from the series sum over m >= 2 of r^m / (m(m-1)). It is tight at r = 1. The code switch at beta = 2.5 is where the interior tau meets 1/beta. The minor's value equals the raw table's value, since T differs by a row constant.
verdicts.counterexample: None to the theorem with beta defined by a sum over layers. The words 'one common beta' have a false reading, where beta is the largest single-layer value. Then splitting a layer into many equal copies drives R to 1/2 and gives E/2. Table: s = [[.92448, .07552], [.99849, .00151]], p = [.00319, .99681], b = [.93282, .06718], k = 0. E/2 = 1.379e-3 exceeds I = L_free(0) = 6.97e-4. The true value is R(2.976) E = 6.15e-4, which is below I.

That 2 x 2 table, 1.13. p3_peel.py uses the sum over layers, so its numbers stand. On photo rows the floor reaches L_on and V_b through TQ11 part 1, L_free <= V_b <= L_on. Coverage does not set the floor: over k = 14 configurations, the Spearman value of coverage against floor is -.52 on ResNet-18 and -.57 on ResNet-50. result.summary: Zero slots are filled, and the main target failed: I have no lower bound on ResNet-18's or ResNet-50's box above the free-code floor at real size, and I prove why four routes to one cannot work. statements.statement: R1 (the box as floor at a span plus a distillation of codes) (under: none; any table with s > 0; V of full column rank modulo 1). For fixed V let (t°, c°) be the least free codes at V, q°_x = softmax(t° + V c°_x), and L_free(V) their loss. For every build with logits t' + V c'_x, gated or not: D = L_free(V) + sum p_x KL(q°_x || softmax(t' + V c'_x)). Hence V_b(k) = min over V of [ L_free(V) + E_b(V) ], with E_b(V) = inf over t', M, beta of sum p KL(q°(V) || softmax(t' + V relu(M z + beta))), and the same form holds for L_on. It is an identity and not a lower bound past L_free(V).
statements.proof: Stationarity of (t°, c°): V^T (s_x - q°_x) = 0 for each row, and sum p (s_x - q°_x) = 0. Then KL(s||q') - KL(s||q°) - KL(q°||q') = <s - q°, log q° - log q'> = <s - q°, l° - l'>, since <s - q°, 1> = 0. Here l° - l' = (t° - t') + V (c° - c'). Summing with p, the t part vanishes by the mean condition and the V part vanishes row by row. This is TZ10's fixed-span identity, stated at any V and any code class. Attainment: s > 0 makes D coercive modulo the kernel at fixed V.

Let lbar_c be the p-mean of l_x on region c, qbar_c = softmax(lbar_c), d_x = l_x - lbar_c, sbar_c the region mean of s. Then D = A + E + N - T, with A = sum pi_c KL(sbar_c || qbar_c), E = sum p KL(s_x || sbar_c), N = sum p K_qbar(d_x) >= 0 where K_q(d) = log E_q e^d - E_q d, and T = sum p <s_x - sbar_c, d_x>. statements.statement: R3 (the signed cut program, and its dual that depends on the competitor's cuts) (under: groups in the last hidden layer; class (b) builds). Rows x, positions s, zeta(x,s) = (1, z(x,s)). For a sign pattern sigma_j with y^j(x,s) = +1 on, -1 off, let F_j(x) = mean over s of 1[on] zeta(x,s). Lambda_+(V, sigma) = least over t, theta_j of D(t + sum_j v_j <F_j(x), theta_j>) subject to y^j(x,s) <zeta(x,s), theta_j> >= 0. This is convex with linear constraints. Then V_b(k) = inf over V, sigma of Lambda_+(V, sigma), exactly. Dual: Lambda_+(V, sigma) = max of sum p [H(r_x) - H(s_x)] over r_x in the simplex and mu >= 0 with sum p (r_x - s_x) = 0 and sum_x p_x <r_x - s_x, v_j> F_j(x) = sum over x,s of mu^j(x,s) y^j(x,s) zeta(x,s) for each j. So each unit's moment must lie in the normal cone of its cut's cell. Dropping the sign constraints (mu = 0) gives Lambda <= Lambda_+, a per-unit sharpening of J4.4 part 2. This removes J's free sign at fixed cuts: the hinge moment is >= 0 on the cell. It does not remove it over all V and sigma.
statements.proof: On the closed cell of sigma, relu(u) = 1[on] u at each position, so the family is exactly the set of builds with that pattern; the union over patterns is the box, which gives the equality. Fenchel: A(l) >= <r, l> + H(r) gives KL(s || softmax l) >= H(r) - H(s) + <r - s, l>. Sum with p. The term linear in theta_j has coefficient equal to the moment. By the dual constraint it equals sum mu y <zeta, theta_j> >= 0 on the cell. Strong duality: D is convex, differentiable and coercive modulo the kernel because s > 0, and the constraints are linear, so KKT holds at the minimiser with r = q. The trivial part is the equality; the content is the dual form.

statements.statement: R4 (four routes that cannot rise above L_free at real size) (under: rows in general affine position in R^D, duplicate rows having the same s). (a) Cells: if k hyperplanes cut P into cells of at most D + 1 rows, the family where the code is affine in z separately on each cell is all free codes, so its least is L_free(k). Real, ResNet-18, 35000 photos, D = 512, 14 random median cuts of mean z: 13117 cells, largest 17 rows, against 513. (b) Fractional cuts: allowing S_j(x) in [0, 1] in c_j(x) = S_j(x) u_j(x) gives exactly all free codes. So any convex relaxation of the gate returns L_free. (c) Small witnesses: on a set T of at most D + 1 rows, V_b on T equals L_free on T, so a witness above L_free needs at least D + 2 = 514 rows at once. That many rows have 2^514 - 2, about 10^154.7, half-space on-sets per unit; 35000 rows have 10^1158.7 per unit, about 10^16200 for 14 units. (d) Span route: min over cuts of [L_inf(Z^S) + L_free(k; q*_S)] <= L_inf(Z) + L_free(k; q*_Z), by the all-on cut. Real, 12000 photos: .0028 + .1797 = .182, while L_free(14) = .184 and the read fit = .904. So the only way above the floor is integer cuts with (m_j, beta_j) shared across at least D + 2 rows, as in R3, and enumeration cannot do that at D = 512.
statements.proof: (a) At most D + 1 affinely independent rows admit any values from an affine function, cell by cell; duplicate rows have the same s and take the same code. (b) Given free codes c, set c' = c - min c >= 0, shift t, take m = 0, beta = max c', S_j(x) = c'_j(x) / beta. The reverse inclusion is trivial. (c) Same as (a) with beta large so all units stay on, and Cover's count 2 sum over i <= D of C(N - 1, i). (d) For the all-on cut, Z^S = Z. Real premise: 12 of 13117 cells are not numerically full rank; each of the 12 contains an exact duplicate photo (distance 0, KL 0).

statements.statement: R6 (a cap on units that are exact on a class) (under: rows of a class share s; z in general position in R^D; V of full column rank modulo 1). If a box build has loss exactly L_free(k), then each unit is positive on at most (D - 1) / (n - 1) classes, for n rows per class. All other classes have code 0 in that unit. So at least K - k floor((D - 1) / (n - 1)) classes share one q = softmax(t). If no free least puts that many classes on one code, then V_b(k) > L_free(k) whenever the infimum is attained. At real size, D = 512, n = 35, K = 1000, k = 14: 15 classes per unit, at most 210 classes on, at least 790 on one code.
statements.proof: KL is strictly convex in the logits modulo 1, so at a free least, rows with the same s have the same code at full rank V. If a unit is on at all rows of class c with positive level, then m_j is orthogonal to the n - 1 within-class differences of c. A class with mixed rows has level 0 on its on rows, so it counts as off. General position makes these difference sets independent up to D, and m_j != 0 requires a total at most D - 1. m_j = 0 is a constant unit that t absorbs. Attainment is not proved: the statement is conditional on it.

If B* in softmax(B* zeta) has full column rank D + 1, every read B' equals Pi B* with Pi = B' (B*)^+, of rank at most k + 1. On real nets q* is within .001 to .006 nats of s, so the k-unit read is, to that error, a fixed low-rank linear map applied to N's own logit vector. result.blocked_by: Any bound above L_free must charge E_b(V) = sum p KL(q°(V) || q) uniformly over all V and all cuts. R3 removes the sign problem only at fixed V and cuts. R4 shows every convex or local relaxation of the cuts falls back to L_free, and full enumeration is 10^1158 per unit. The missing tool is a uniform statement of this form: no rank-k fixed linear encoder, or k half-space units, can write the free code of a table whose rows have many different Fisher metrics. Such a statement must see at least 514 rows at once and must hold with no weight cap. No referee has read these statements, and they have no Lean line.

verdicts.statement: Q-A (the fixed-V dual, and H1's row cap is the same set).
verdicts.false_step: None in the theorem. One loose sentence: 'as the referee found'. The round 2 referee recorded that H1(b) admits no v0 on either row set. The referee did not record a negative value for this envelope. The arithmetic does give a negative value: hbar is 2.13 and m is .37, so (m + 1) v0 - hbar is below 0 at small v0.
verdicts.counterexample: None. Small tables, fixed V, 8 tables: |primal - dual| is at most 2.1e-9, |V^T r| at most 2.4e-7.
verdicts.gaps: I checked each step by hand. Gibbs gives the lower side. The Lagrangian in (t, c) is finite only under the two constraints. q° = s is a strictly positive feasible point, so there is no gap. The H1 change of variables is R_xi = y_xi - p_x mu_xi = (p_x / e)(q°_xi - s_xi), and q° >= 0 is exactly y >= 0 with e y_x <= p_x. The real-table 'dual value' .24509 is not a feasible dual value, because the residual is 4.3e-3. The author says it is not a bound. The H1 envelope does not strictly drop the entropy. It replaces the entropy by a worst-case term.

verdicts.statement: Q-C (the weighted rectangle dual, computable at any k), with uses Q1, Q5 and Q7.
verdicts.false_step: None.
verdicts.counterexample: None found. 24 small tables with non-flat W, non-flat gamma and unequal p: 0 violations against 5 random fits and aimed fits, and h >= -rho at every aimed competitor. This test is weak, because the bound was above 0 on only 5 of 24 tables and reached at most .007 of the best fit. On real tables, 200 sampled rectangles on each net: certified value <= the L-BFGS rectangle least on every one.
verdicts.gaps: I checked every step by hand. psi >= 0, so dropping weight is safe. D = sum n psi(e) uses sum q = sum s = 1. L_x on S lies in span(t_S, V_S, 1_S), of dimension at most k + 2, and that span times gamma contains gamma. <Y_x, L_x> = 0. Q-B gives h >= -rho. psi*(h) / h^2 falls on (-1, inf), so kap(rho) is valid. tr(Pi B) with B zero on gamma gives tr B minus the k + 1 largest positive eigenvalues. Slices telescope to at most s. Q7 weights are valid in q8_tree.py. Floating-point eigenvalues are not interval-checked. The photo table is clamped at 1e-13, so the photo floor is on the clamped table. The change to the true table should be about 1e-10 relative, but I did not compute it. The label table has no entry under the clamp on R18. The smallest entry on R50 is 1.4e-10, so the clamp is not active there.
verdicts.corrected_statement: As stated. Covers free codes on any rows. On photo rows it also covers the read and the box through V_b >= L_free. It is not a slot result.

verdicts.false_step: None.

This does not show that a Q1 system reaches .14. (2) One shared set of 14 units, aimed at the covered weights by L-BFGS, 1500 iterations. A rectangle dual that also uses the real normaliser (sum of q on S at most 1) is outside the theorem. The gap .00384 against .00251 may mark room there, but both are upper values. So on the author's Q5 weights any projector dual, one projector or many, linear or not, is at most .00251 on R18 (.0102 of the fit) and .00155 on R50 (.0083). verdicts.statement: R1. For any build at span V: D = L_free(V) + sum p KL(q° || q'). Hence V_b(k) = min over V of [L_free(V) + E_b(V)].
verdicts.false_step: Only the word 'min'. The identity itself holds and I checked each step. It is TZ10's fixed-span identity, so it is not new.
verdicts.counterexample: Six rows z = -2,-1,0,1,2,3 on a line, K = 3, k = 2. r = relu(z), w = (0,0,1/2,1,1,1), L = a r^T + b w^T with a, b independent mod 1. Exact elimination over all on-sets: the only unit codes in span(1, r, w) are multiples of r and constants, so no 2-unit build has D = 0. Units relu(z + eps), relu(z - eps) give D = .00016, 1.6e-6, 1.6e-8, 1.6e-10 at eps = .1 to 1e-4, with |V| about 1/eps. So V_b(2) = 0 and it is not attained. This table only corrects the wording. It is not a result.
verdicts.gaps: none on the identity. Numeric check on real rows: sum check -2.4e-5 in float64.
verdicts.corrected_statement: V_b(k) = inf over V of [L_free(V) + E_b(V)]. At fixed V the inner infimum is attained: each unit's code set is a finite union of polyhedral cones, so the logit set is a finite union of polyhedra, and D is coercive modulo constants at s > 0. Only the outer infimum can fail.

verdicts.statement: R4. (a) cells, (b) fractional cuts and 'any convex relaxation returns L_free', (c) small witnesses, (d) span route. Then: the only way above the floor is integer cuts shared across at least D + 2 rows, and enumeration cannot do that.
verdicts.false_step: Parts (a), (c), (d) and the first part of (b) hold. Two sentences do not follow. 'Any convex relaxation' is not proved by one relaxation with free S. 'The only way' is a claim about all routes, and only four were treated.
verdicts.counterexample: Against 'only way': the author's own R6 reaches strictness by dimension count with no enumeration. Numbers in (d): .182 < .184 compares unequal effort. At equal schedule, 12000 rows: L_free(14; s) at most .1659 and B at most .1723, so B sits above L_free by about .006 on fit values. It stays useless against .90. Numbers in (c): the box cuts act at 1715000 positions, so the count is about 10^2025 per unit and not 10^1158, which only strengthens the point.
verdicts.gaps: The vertex premise below is checked by a sufficient test on a sample only: 1997 of 2000 pooled rows pass on 35000 rows, one failure is an exact duplicate, and two are unresolved. The position form was not tested.
verdicts.corrected_statement: Lemma that makes (b) true. If each row (or, for the position box, some position of each row) is a vertex of the convex hull of all rows (positions), then a single unit can give e_x times any positive level. So the convex hull of the unit code set is all nonnegative codes. Any relaxation that replaces the code set at fixed V by a convex superset then returns L_free. Proof: hinge at the vertex, then take conic sums, then absorb the constant in t. Routes other than these four stay open.

verdicts.statement: R6. Box build at loss exactly L_free(k), rows of a class share s, z in general position: each unit is positive on at most (D - 1)/(n - 1) classes, and at least K - k floor((D - 1)/(n - 1)) classes share one q. V_b(k) > L_free(k) if the infimum is attained and no free least has this.
verdicts.false_step: 'General position makes these difference sets independent up to D.' General position of rows does not give that. Also the K = 4 'check' checks nothing: there D = 4, n = 2 gives cap 3, so K - 3 = 1 class on t, which any code meets after a shift. Also a constant unit (m = 0) is positive on all classes, so 'each unit' needs m != 0.
verdicts.counterexample: D = 2, n = 2, K = 3. Rows A (0,0),(1,0), B (0,1),(1,1), C (.5,-1),(3,-1). No three rows are collinear. All within-class differences are parallel to e1. Unit m = (0,1), beta = 2 has levels 2, 3, 1, positive on 3 classes against a cap of 1. Any s that depends only on the second coordinate, with k = 1, has L_free(1) = 0 reached by this unit. Three classes have three distinct q, against the claimed 2 on one q.
verdicts.gaps: The premise that s is constant on classes fails on real tables (eps_const .50). The form below gives no number. It covers one position per row. For the position box the same count needs independence of the F_j differences at each pattern. t9 (k = 2, D = 1, n = 2, 400 starts): least fit .0127, above L_free = 0, which is consistent. Its value is far below the .2688 of a build with two classes on one code, so the count gives strictness only and not a value.
verdicts.corrected_statement: Replace the premise. (G) Within-class differences of any set of classes are independent up to D, and any D + 1 rows are affinely independent. Then the cap holds for units with m != 0. Stronger form, with NO attainment needed, one position per row, L_free(k) < L_free(k - 1), K(n - 1) >= D: if V_b(k) = L_free(k), some free least has at least K - k floor((D - 1)/(n - 1)) - floor(kD/n) classes on one code. At D = 512, n = 35, k = 14 this is 1000 - 210 - 204 = 586. Proof: take builds with D -> L_free(k). Logits converge along a subsequence to a free least L*, class-constant by strict convexity. By the strict drop, code spaces W_i = span(1, c^i) converge to W = col(L*) + span(1). Fix on-sets O_j and take unit limits theta_j^0. If m_0 = 0: beta_0 < 0 makes c = 0, and beta_0 > 0 makes c affine, so its unit limit m_1 . z lies in W, against K(n - 1) >= D. So m_0 != 0. The limit relu(u_0) is in W and so is class-constant, which gives a_j classes on with a_j(n - 1) <= D - 1. Rows with u_0 = 0 number at most D. On rows outside all O_j every element of W_i is constant, hence every element of W too. A class with no such row meets some positive set or has all n rows on boundaries, at most kD/n classes in total. This proof is by hand and has had no second reader.

verdicts.statement: R7. A gate that switches off one row gains at most p KL(s || q). Real sizes .00048 and .00021. A gate helps by a real amount only if one half-space isolates hundreds of rows of high loss.
verdicts.false_step: The cap holds (KL >= 0, one row changes). The last sentence does not follow: the cap covers gates with no refit. It does not cover off sets inside photos, with V and M refitted.
verdicts.counterexample: The refined gated fit on 35000 rows has 16 percent of positions off, and a unit is fully off on only 6e-5 of sealed photo-unit pairs. So it isolates no rows. It is not below the read, so it does not show a real gain. It shows the mechanism is of another kind.
verdicts.gaps: Pooled z, read residual, logistic fit, 300 iterations: one half-space isolates the top 50 loss rows with 0 wrong (.0077 of the loss). At 100 rows it takes in 288 other rows. This is not a proof of non-separability. My prediction of about 400 rows was wrong.
verdicts.corrected_statement: A no-refit gate on a row set T gains at most the sum over T of p KL. On the read at 12000 rows, 344 rows are needed for .1 nat. Measured: one hinge touching 270 rows gains 3.3e-4. Gates at position level with refit are not covered.

verdicts.statement: R8. If B* has full column rank D + 1, every read is Pi B* with Pi of rank at most k + 1, and L_Z(k) = L_inf + the least over such Pi. On real nets, to that error, the k-unit read is a fixed low-rank linear map applied to N's own logit vector.
verdicts.false_step: Three steps. (1) The premise is impossible on ResNet-50: B* is 1000 x 2049, and its rank modulo 1 is at most 999. (2) 'To that error' is a non sequitur: KL(s || q*) small does not control Pi (l* - y), because Pi can be large. (3) 'Rank at most k + 1' is necessary only. All rank k + 1 matrices allow reads with k + 1 units and zero t, which is a larger family.
verdicts.counterexample: ResNet-18, 12000 rows. Pi from the read: |Pi|_2 = 217, and Pi l* reproduces D = .90405. The same Pi on N's centred logits y gives D = 7.35 on fit rows and 8.36 on sealed rows, against 1.945 for the read. rms(l* - y) is .58. Best rank-14 read of y itself: .853 fit and 1.735 sealed, against .8998 and 1.955 for the read of z. That is a different family, separated by more than the .003 'error'.
verdicts.gaps: The rank premise is now checked on ResNet-18: rank 513, smallest singular value .196 after centring, largest 30.
verdicts.corrected_statement: ResNet-18 only: every read is exactly Pi applied to the full read's logits l*, with Pi B*^T of the form t e_0 + V N. L_Z(k) = L_inf + the least over such Pi of the mean KL(q* || softmax(Pi l*)). Nothing is claimed about Pi on N's logits.

verdicts.statement: R-F1. No number above L_free(k) bounds V_b(k), and none bounds L_on(k) over all V, at real size. K = 4 shows the gap is real.

verdicts.counterexample: none. I found no such bound either. TZ10 gives L_on(14) >= L_inf + L_free(14; q*), and those parts are upper values (.1723), so this is not a certified number. It is under one fifth of the read.
verdicts.gaps: About .73 nats on 12000 rows stay uncharged between the floor (at most .166) and the best box fit (at most .8995). Both are upper values, so this gap is itself not certified.
verdicts.corrected_statement: Open. The gap is measured on fits only. No certified lower bound on V_b above a certified L_free exists on real rows.

result.slots_really_filled: None, and I agree with the author on this. L_inf is the nearest to slot 1, and it does not fill it. It names one layer and one read form. Its fit-row error is partly row count, since it is exactly 0 at n <= D + 1, and its held-out error is 10 times the fit value. It says nothing on rank. R1 to R3 are identities. R6 in the corrected form is a strictness statement with no number, and its premise (s constant on classes) fails on real tables (eps_const .50). The author also said this is not a theorem that a slot cannot be filled, and that is correct. R4 limits proof routes only, and two of its sentences overreach.
result.real_network_test: Main number. Re-run in float64 with separate code on the same 12000 ResNet-18 rows. The identity holds: .90404 = .24616 + .65786, sum check -2.4e-5. The values do not hold as converged values. All are upper values, and each one moved. Read on 12000 rows: .9040 to .8998 (270 s). Floor L_free(14): .1837 to at most .1659. Span term: .062 to at least .080. B: .182 to at most .1723. Read on 35000 rows: 1.1723 to 1.1720. ResNet-50 read at k = 14: .528 to .515. L_inf fit values reproduce (.0028, .0039, .0060, ResNet-50 .0006), with held-out values .034, .033, .028, .0062. The r11 box run stalled after 60 iterations in float32, so its '2220 iterations' are not real work, and it tests no gate. New on real rows: one hinge gives .89948, below the read at .89981. Saved random-start box, refined on 35000 rows: 1.258 to 1.192, on share .826 to .843, sealed 1.519, still above the read (1.172, sealed 1.488), still falling. Pi applied to N's logits: 7.35 against .904. Ratio at k = 512: at least 30. The author's main conclusion holds: no lower bound above L_free exists at real size, and about .73 nats stay uncharged. Own predictions that failed: read of y above .904 (it was .853), isolation near 400 rows (at most about 50 clean), t9 value equal to the two-class build (it was far below).
